bound_direction_down: gold in fog is scored as zero, so genuinely reachable fogged gold is never credited
an invisible enemy could block a planned step; the model cannot see it (affects base and oracle identically)
bound_direction_up: the oracle re-optimises from a position the base's own strategy chose, so it inherits free positioning it did not pay for
biases.decomposition_direction: the cause1/cause2 split is round-classification based; a unit-round is labelled by the base's own action pattern, so the split is exact and additive but the LABEL is a statement about the base's state, not about the mechanism of the gain.
biases.local_baseline_absolutes: local seat-1 net income is 1122-1725 (self-play against a full-strength copy of ourselves), far below the platform's 2182.4 uncontested figure against the passive probeobs probe. Local absolutes are NOT ceilings.
biases.npc_model: the local NPC model matches real NPC actions only 38.7% of the time and is over-greedy/over-centralised; absolute income is NOT comparable to the platform, only same-seed paired deltas are. Income from central-efficiency changes is SYSTEMATICALLY UNDER-estimated here.

fast_path_equivalence.coverage: sampled every 41st round of all 15 games, 65 rounds per map
fast_path_equivalence.reference: exhaustive joint_outcomes: 125 first-unit sequences x 125 second-unit sequences = 15625 pairs per round, dict-copying simulate_unit
fast_path_equivalence.speedup_note: fast path runs the full six-search decomposition in ~4.4 s per 500-round game including the engine itself

fog_guarantee: The oracle never sees a latent value: the array it reads is the engine's own fog-filtered grid, so a fogged gold amount is absent, not merely unused. fog_discipline() additionally asserts every gold value entering the model lies inside the radius-2 visibility union of the seat's own two units; it ran on every 50th round of all 15 games and never fired.

harness.opponent: the same frozen build in seat 2 (local self-play)
harness.seat: player 1 is the faster mover, so it settles before every NPC and before player 2; the counterfactual board is therefore the exact board the seat acts on

static wall table of the map (the frozen build fingerprints and locks the identical table by round 4)
bombs remembered from earlier rounds of the current 20-round bomb wave, purged when a currently visible cell proves the bomb is gone

round_level_check.note: the base action's value under the information-constrained model reproduces the engine exactly, round by round

open_loop_trajectory_identity.evidence: for all 15 games the measurement run's log_sha256 equals the plain baseline run's log_sha256 for the same map and seed
open_loop_trajectory_identity.mechanism: the shim calls moveDecision and returns its six actions, k, order and vp verbatim

question: gold/game the frozen one-target walker leaves on the table by not choosing the best visible three-step path

resolution: The raw quantity is a per-round counterfactual summed over 500 rounds. Gold is a STOCK, not a flow: crediting the oracle for a cell in round r while the base's own trajectory harvests that same cell in round r+k double-counts.
The stock/flow split shows 85-92% of the raw bound is exactly that timing double-count; only 78-145 gold/game is on cells the base never re-enters for the rest of the game.
The closed-loop check settles it: playing the oracle actually LOSES 738-894 gold/game, and even the cheapest ladder rung (re-choosing only the third step) is -65 +/- 74 gold/game pooled.
So the bound does not imply T-1 leaves ~500 gold unclaimed. It implies a per-round three-step path optimum is not a realizable income channel for either side.
